target_customer: Online shoppers in the US who want refunds when items they bought drop in price
problem: Many retailers promise price adjustments but shoppers rarely notice price drops or file claims. Paribus scanned receipts and filed claims for them.
business_model: Free to users with a share of recovered savings (later users kept 100 percent after the Capital One acquisition)
product_category: Consumer price tracking and refund automation

founders.name: Karim Atiyeh
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; later founded Ramp with Eric Glyman.

founders.name: Eric Glyman
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO by TechCrunch (2015-10-07); not listed on the YC page opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing email receipts across many retailers, tracking prices and filing claims with varying policies was standard engineering with messy integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Retailer policies were public and the method was copyable, and Earny launched a similar subscription service; early user growth and receipt data gave limited edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Capital One, a card issuer, bought Paribus in October 2016 and folded it into shopping features; Capital One ended price protection in January 2023.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2015-10-07) reported nearly 50,000 customers within months of launch with double digit weekly growth, and projected protecting over $100 million in purchases per year.

branding.domain_note: Used paribus.co, which now redirects to capitaloneshopping.com.

rebrands.why: Folded into Capital One after acquisition; site paribus.co redirects there

branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch (2015-10-07) reported about half of sign ups shared it, driving referral growth.

brand_strength.rationale: Referral driven growth to 700,000 users but no sourced coverage of the brand itself, and the name was absorbed after the sale.

outcome_analysis: Paribus grew through referrals to nearly 50,000 customers by October 2015 and over 700,000 by its sale, raising only $2.22 million. Capital One acquired it in October 2016 with undisclosed terms, hiring the 12 person team, and later ended price protection in January 2023. The edge was speed and a clear consumer benefit, not a structural moat.
notes: YC page has no description or website; paribus.co redirected to capitaloneshopping.com. Total funding $2.22M stated by TechCrunch at the acquisition, hence complete coverage. Aggregators disagree on the lead (Seedtable says Conversion Capital); TechCrunch says General Catalyst. Earny launched later as a similar service and is not recorded as a founding competitor; no dated 2015 competitor sources opened. Name origin is reported in Wikipedia as the Latin phrase ceteris paribus, but that line is uncited and the page was not opened. Founders' education (a search summary says Harvard) not verified.
